metaData.originalTitle: Towards Speed-of-Light Text Generation with Nemotron-Labs Diffusion Language Models
metaData.title: Towards Speed-of-Light Text Generation with Nemotron-Labs Diffusion Language Models
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: NVIDIA's Nemotron-Labs Diffusion introduces a family of language models that combine autoregressive and diffusion-based generation, enabling parallel token drafting and iterative refinement for significantly faster text generation while maintaining accuracy.
metaData.summary: This article from the Hugging Face Blog announces NVIDIA's Nemotron-Labs Diffusion, a new family of language models that break away from purely autoregressive generation. The key innovation is a tri-mode design: standard autoregressive mode for compatibility, a diffusion mode that generates and refines tokens in parallel blocks for high throughput, and a self-speculation mode that uses diffusion to draft tokens and autoregressive decoding to verify them, achieving lossless acceleration. The models (3B, 8B, 14B text, 8B VLM) are trained by adding diffusion capabilities to a pre-trained autoregressive model, allowing them to retain learned knowledge while gaining parallel generation. Performance highlights include the 8B model achieving 1.2% better average accuracy than Qwen3 8B and up to 6.4x higher tokens-per-forward-pass in self-speculation mode. The models are open-source under a commercially-friendly license and will be deployable via SGLang, allowing developers to switch between generation modes with a single configuration change.

mainPoints.point: Nemotron-Labs Diffusion models support three generation modes in a single model: autoregressive, diffusion, and self-speculation.
mainPoints.explanation: This tri-mode design allows developers to choose between standard AR compatibility, high-throughput parallel generation via diffusion, or lossless acceleration via self-speculation, all from the same checkpoint.

mainPoints.point: The diffusion and self-speculation modes achieve significant speedups over pure autoregressive models.
mainPoints.explanation: The 8B model achieves up to 6.4x higher tokens-per-forward-pass in self-speculation mode and 2.6x in diffusion mode, while maintaining comparable or better accuracy than strong AR baselines like Qwen3 8B.

mainPoints.point: The models are trained by adding diffusion capabilities to an existing autoregressive model through continued pretraining.
mainPoints.explanation: This approach, building on Efficient-DLM research, preserves the knowledge from AR training while enabling parallel drafting and iterative refinement, making the training process more practical and stable.

keyQuotes: Nemotron-Labs Diffusion is designed around a simple idea: autoregressive and diffusion generation should not be separate model families. They should be capabilities of the same model.
By reducing the number of refinement steps, one can reduce the compute requirements of these models at runtime.
Self-speculation mode uses diffusion to draft multiple candidate tokens, then uses autoregressive decoding to verify them.
Output is lossless versus AR at temperature 0, but we hit ~865 tok/s on B200 on speedbench dataset - roughly 4× the autoregressive baseline on the same hardware.

relatedArticles.title: OpenAI Secures $110 Billion Funding from Amazon, NVIDIA, and SoftBank
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Sam Altman announces a historic $110 billion funding round for OpenAI backed by Amazon, NVIDIA, and SoftBank.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano Omni: Long-Context Multimodal Intelligence for Documents， Audio and Video Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: NVIDIA introduces Nemotron 3 Nano Omni, a new open-weight omni-modal model that combines text, image, video, and audio understanding with a hybrid Mamba-Transformer-MoE backbone, achieving top accuracy on multiple multimodal leaderboards while delivering up to 9x higher throughput.

relatedArticles.title: Building a Fast Multilingual OCR Model with Synthetic Data
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details NVIDIA's development of Nemotron OCR v2, a fast and accurate multilingual OCR model trained on a massive, open-source synthetic dataset of 12.2 million images, overcoming data scarcity through a scalable, language-agnostic rendering pipeline.

relatedArticles.title: How NVIDIA AI-Q Reached \#1 on DeepResearch Bench I and II
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: NVIDIA AI-Q achieves state-of-the-art performance on deep research benchmarks through a modular multi-agent architecture, fine-tuned Nemotron-3 models, and specialized reliability middleware.

relatedArticles.title: Achieving Single-Digit Microsecond Latency Inference for Capital Markets
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how NVIDIA achieves record-breaking single-digit microsecond latency for LSTM-based inference in algorithmic trading using custom CUDA kernels and hardware-specific optimizations on GH200 and Blackwell GPUs.

relatedArticles.title: Jensen Huang: NVIDIA - The $4 Trillion Company & the AI Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #494
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: 黄仁勋在访谈中深入探讨了从芯片到「AI 工厂」的计算演进、极限协同设计方法论、AI 四大扩展定律以及 NVIDIA 以 CUDA 装机量为核心的竞争护城河。

relatedArticles.title: Specialization Beats Scale: A Strategic Variable Most AI Procurement Decisions Overlook
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A 3-billion-parameter specialized model outperformed every commercial frontier API in a structured OCR benchmark at roughly fifty times lower cost, demonstrating that distributional alignment to the deployment task can be more decisive than parameter count.

relatedArticles.title: Falcon Perception
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Falcon Perception is a 0.6B early-fusion Transformer that unifies vision and language in a single backbone for open-vocabulary grounding and segmentation, outperforming SAM 3 on complex compositional prompts.

relatedArticles.title: Robotics' End Game: Nvidia's Jim Fan
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: NVIDIA's Jim Fan argues that robotics will follow the scaling path of LLMs through world models, egocentric human video, neural simulators, World Action Models, and real-to-sim-to-real data pipelines.

relatedArticles.title: NVIDIA and Partners Open-Source CaP-X for Agentic Robotics
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Jim Fan introduces CaP-X, a comprehensive open-source framework and benchmark suite designed to enable LLMs to synthesize code for robot perception and control.
